archetype.name: Playoff Team (shooting-first)
archetype.definition: A team whose top-five margin rests on an elite-shooting backcourt and strong rebounding, good enough to play into the postseason even if the hot shooting cools.

report.headline: A real turnaround, though its shooting runs ahead of what the roster can hold
report.take:
Memphis went 25-57 last season and ranked 26th on the site. Thirteen games into this one it is 9-4 with a Net Rtg of 8.9, fifth in the league, built on an offense rated 120.4 (4th) and a defense rated 111.5 (8th). This is not a record that ran ahead of its play. The W vs Pt Diff is -1, and the margin implies 10 wins rather than nine. The scoring margin is real. The open question is how much of it comes from shooting the roster can't sustain.

The engine is the backcourt, graded A. Cedric Coward is second of 109 on the shooting guard tab, and the team is +16.3 per 100 with him on the floor. Ty Jerome carries the heaviest load with a 31.8 USG % and the most points on the roster. Cam Spencer has been absurdly efficient: a 74.2 TS % and a 5.6 BPM. Together they produce 3P % of 39.2, second in the league and four points above the league mean, on a slightly above-average share of threes. The other pillar is the glass: REB % of 53.2 ranks 3rd, with top-seven marks on both ends. That has been a Memphis trait in its good seasons before. This roster is the 2021-22 team's rebounding with a modern shot diet.

What the numbers hide is thinness and fragility. The wings grade D+, and Kris Murray's 28.7 TS % is the main wing minutes. Cameron Boozer leads the team in minutes and usage but shoots a 50.8 TS %, and the team is -9.4 with him on. Jerome is listed out, and Edey and Stewart are day-to-day, so the most efficient creator and the rim presence are both in question. The defense has held opponents to 33 % from three without forcing turnovers (Opp TOV % ranks 23rd). The first trait usually drifts back toward the league, and the second gives it no cushion when that happens.

The October 6-0 came against Utah, Portland and Sacramento types, allowing 106 a game. November was 3-4, allowing 116.57, with losses to OKC, Denver and Indiana. Even so, the offense never dipped, and the last two games were blowouts. Expect a team that is clearly good rather than elite. It stays a playoff team as long as the guards stay healthy.

strengths.title: Backcourt shooting carries the offense
strengths.body: Coward, Spencer, Jerome and Wells give Memphis an A backcourt, and their shooting drives a top-four offense. Some of it will cool: Spencer's TS % is not a sustainable number, and no recent Memphis team shot near this well from three. The shot quality and the depth of shooters should keep the offense well above average even as the hot percentages fade.

strengths.title: Coward drives the lineup math
strengths.body: Coward is the roster's best ranked player at his position, and his On-Off dwarfs everyone else's among regulars. He rebounds well for a guard, which helps tie the rebounding and shooting identities together. A two-way impact like this tends to hold up better than a pure shooting spike.

strengths.title: Winning the glass at both ends
strengths.body: Memphis ranks 3rd in REB % and top seven in both offensive and defensive rebounding. That gives it extra possessions and limits opponents to one shot. Rebounding is a stable, structural trait, and it was a hallmark of the franchise's best recent seasons. It should travel.

concerns.title: Injuries hit the key pieces
concerns.body: Jerome, the team's top usage and scoring guard, is out, and both centers, Edey and Stewart, are day-to-day. Edey's On-Off is strongly positive, so his absence costs real rim presence. Without Jerome, more creation falls to Boozer, whose efficiency so far can't carry that load.

concerns.title: Defense leaning on opponent misses
concerns.body: The Def Rank of 8 comes with opponents shooting well below the league from three. Meanwhile the defense forces few turnovers. Opponent 3-point shooting is mostly noise over a small sample, and points allowed per game have already climbed from October to November. Expect the defense to settle closer to the middle of the league.

concerns.title: No real wing rotation
concerns.body: The wings grade D+, and the listed small forwards have barely played or barely scored. Murray's shooting is a liability. That pushes guards and power forwards into mismatched roles, and it gets exposed against teams with big, scoring wings.

trend.note: The 6-0 October came against soft opponents, and November cooled to 3-4 as the defense slipped. Scoring held level the whole way, and the last two games were lopsided wins, so the margin has barely moved.

weekAhead.headline: Two soft road dates bracket a demanding Cleveland-Golden State-Minnesota run
weekAhead.body:
Memphis opens at Washington and closes at Charlotte. Both are bottom-tier teams with weak offenses, and both should be wins if the shooting shows up. The middle of the week is harder. Cleveland and Golden State come on consecutive nights, and both have top-eight offenses. Then comes a trip to Minnesota, which shares Memphis's 9-4 record and has the league's best defense.

The week is mostly on the road, and Jerome is out with the centers uncertain. A 3-2 week would be par, and 4-1 would mean the offense is holding up without its lead creator. The Minnesota game is the truest measure: its defense shuts down threes and forwards, exactly where Memphis lives and where it is thin.

keyMatchups.title: Shooting against Minnesota's top defense
keyMatchups.body: Minnesota has the league's best defensive rating and holds opponents to 32.5 % from three. That is the most direct test yet of whether Memphis's shooting is skill or a hot start. If Memphis wins the glass there, it can survive a cold night.

keyMatchups.title: Rim chances against Golden State
keyMatchups.body: Golden State's frontcourt grades F, and opponents shoot very well at its rim. It is the spot to lean on Edey or Stewart if either is cleared. Golden State also leads the league in 3P %, so Memphis has to win inside rather than trade threes.

keyMatchups.title: Guards against leaky perimeter defenses
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland gives up a lot to shooting guards, and Charlotte allows the highest opponent 3-point percentage in the league. Both suit Coward, Wells and Spencer while Jerome sits.

weekAhead.watch: Who creates when Jerome is out: whether Coward and Spencer absorb the load efficiently, or whether it falls to Boozer's low-efficiency volume.

restOfSeason.body:
The foundation is real. The margin supports the record, the rebounding is structural, and the backcourt has quality beyond one hot shooter. The shooting won't stay this good. Spencer's efficiency and a near-league-best 3P % will regress, and opponents won't keep missing threes at this rate. That points to an offensive rating closer to 116-119 and a Net Rtg in the low-to-mid single digits. That is still clearly a playoff team, just not on the 57-win pace the early margin implies. A final range of 46-52 wins fits.

The biggest variables are health and structure. Jerome and both centers are already on the injury report. The wing rotation is close to nonexistent, and Boozer's efficiency needs to rise if he keeps this much of the ball. If the guards stay healthy and Boozer grows into his role, the top of the range is reachable. Lose the backcourt depth and this slides toward the play-in.
swingFactors: Jerome's return and health of the A backcourt
How far the 3-point shooting regresses on both ends

confidence.note: Thirteen games, and the shooting looks unsustainable, but the margin and rebounding support the record.
